profile.campus: Rowan Percheron Data Center Campus (Morrow County, OR)
profile.reading: This record is one of four tightly clustered OSM buildings this registry maps as "Percheron DC," on Tower Road in Morrow County, Oregon, approximately nine miles south of Interstate 84. Morrow County's own Planning Commission records confirm a real, government-processed land use case for this site: case numbers AC-145-23 (Comprehensive Plan amendment), ACM-146-23, and AZM-147-23 (zone map amendment), filed by applicant Rowan Percheron, LLC, seeking to rezone approximately 274 acres from Exclusive Farm Use (EFU) to General Industrial (MG) with a Limited Use Overlay Zone restricting development to data center operations only, evaluated under Morrow County Zoning Ordinance Article 8 and Oregon Administrative Rules 660-004-0010, including exceptions to Statewide Planning Goals 3 (Farmland), 11 (Public Facilities), and 14 (Urbanization). The case record, adopted by the Planning Commission, references a land use application, soils/geotechnical/wetland delineation reports, a traffic impact analysis and economic analysis summary, endangered-species and cultural-resource assessments, a water supply memorandum of understanding with the Port of Morrow, and correspondence with the Navy and area tribes, indicating a substantial, real industrial-scale project rather than a speculative or nominal filing. Morrow County has become one of Oregon's most significant data center corridors in recent years, anchored by a large Amazon build-out reported in 2022 at roughly $12 billion across at least five facilities, and the water-supply coordination with the Port of Morrow reflects the same regional water-availability questions that have drawn scrutiny to other large data center projects in the county. No building-specific square footage, MW capacity, or year-opened figure for this particular building was located in county planning materials or any operator website reachable this session; Rowan Green Data LLC and Rowan Percheron, LLC appear, per the county's own case record, to be closely related entities behind the same Tower Road project, though this registry has not independently confirmed the precise legal relationship between the two names.

profile.legal_name: Rowan Green Data LLC, DBA Rowan Digital Infrastructure
profile.research_note: Operator's own site (rowandigitalinfrastructure.com) returned a 521 server error this session; facts sourced instead from Quinbrook's own press release on the Rowan platform. That release focused on the Temple, Texas campus and did not mention the Morrow County, Oregon site this registry's facility rows are tagged to; Oregon operations not independently confirmed against a primary Rowan or Quinbrook source this session, only via trade press (Data Center Dynamics) and a local chamber-of-commerce business listing.
profile.oregon_project: Trade press (Data Center Dynamics) separately reports Rowan planning a 1 million sq ft data center campus in Morrow County, Oregon; local business registration confirms Rowan Green Data LLC DBA Rowan Digital Infrastructure as a Boardman, Oregon area chamber of commerce member
profile.flagship_campus: 800 MW multi-tenant campus in Temple, Texas, first phase 220 MW, nearing construction completion as of a January 2023 announcement

reading:
Rowan Green Data LLC, doing business as Rowan Digital Infrastructure, began in 2020 as a joint venture between Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners and Birch Infrastructure, created to deliver low-cost, renewables-powered land solutions to data center operators. It is now a wholly owned portfolio company of Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners, headquartered in San Francisco, California.

Quinbrook's own press release describes Rowan's flagship project as an 800 megawatt multi-tenant campus in Temple, Texas, with a 220 megawatt first phase nearing construction completion as of a January 2023 announcement, and states the platform has expanded to more than 20 strategically positioned host sites across the United States. That release did not mention Oregon operations directly. Separately, trade press from Data Center Dynamics reports Rowan planning a 1 million square foot data center campus in Morrow County, Oregon, and a Boardman, Oregon area chamber of commerce business listing confirms Rowan Green Data LLC, DBA Rowan Digital Infrastructure, as a registered member there.

The registry here tracks 4 Rowan facilities, all in Oregon, in the same Morrow County, Columbia River hydropower corridor already carrying Meta, Google, and Amazon buildout recorded elsewhere in this registry. Given Rowan's stated business model of providing power and land solutions to other data center operators rather than always operating end-user compute itself, this registry's facility-level research phase should check whether these Oregon sites are Rowan-operated facilities or Rowan-developed land later operated by a tenant.
